properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 28 at 1:03PM EDT until August 28 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Atlantic County in southern New Jersey...

* Until 500 PM EDT.

* At 103 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Atlantic City, Ocean City, Pleasantville, Somers Point, Ventnor
City, Brigantine, Northfield, Absecon, Margate City, Egg Harbor
City, Weymouth and Estell Manor.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 28 at 10:56AM CDT until August 28 at 12:30PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out
20 NM...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 1230 PM CDT.

* At 1055 AM CDT, strong thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 6 nm northeast
of Oriskany Reef to 13 nm southwest of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef,
moving east at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Okaloosa Deep Water Reef.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out 20 NM; Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 28 at 11:00AM CDT until August 28 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 100 PM CDT.

* At 1100 AM CDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 13 nm
southwest of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef to 42 nm southeast of
Oriskany Reef to 67 nm west of Empire Mica Wreck, moving east at 15
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Laguna Beach, Santa Rosa Beach, and Panama City Beach.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 28 at 9:43AM CDT until August 30 at 4:36AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Illinois...

Wabash River from Hutsonville to Vincennes.

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crest. Flooding should come to an end on
the Wabash during the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Agricultural lands and some oil fields
flood.  Several township roads about 1.25 miles south of St.
Francesville and River Road between Billett Road and Lincoln
Memorial Bridge in Lawrence County are flooded.  Extensive flooding
of Kimmell Park at Vincennes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM CDT /9:45 AM EDT/ Friday the stage was 18.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 AM CDT /9:45 AM EDT/ Friday was 18.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 4.6 feet Monday,
September 07.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 945 PM CDT /1045 PM
EDT/.
